raw_response:
I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father farmed it before me. I know what this soil wants, and I know what the market expects from me.

**My reasoning:**

Quzhou is wheat-corn country. That is what the land is suited for, what the buyers come for, and what I know how to grow. My two sons work in Shijiazhuang now, so it is mostly me and my wife. I cannot manage too many mu anymore, and I cannot be trying complicated new things at my age. I have about 10 mu of flat irrigated land. I will put all of it in winter wheat this autumn after I plant summer corn on it now — the same rotation I have done every year of my adult life.

For wheat, I buy improved variety seed from the county seed station — Kenong 199 or whatever the station recommends this year. Not the most expensive hybrid experiment seed. I know this variety, it performs reliably here. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at jointing. I water four times: once before sowing if the soil is dry, once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray for weeds in late winter and treat for aphids and rust at heading. Rotary tillage before sowing.

For corn, I sow hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June — you must use hybrid for corn, everyone does, the yield difference is too large. I direct-seed into the wheat stubble with the machine — no ploughing needed. Summer rains usually help, so I only pump once, maybe at tasseling if it is dry. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and chase with urea at the big bell stage. One herbicide pass after emergence, one spray if I see armyworm.

I will not try anything new this year. At 64, a bad gamble on a new crop is a gamble I cannot afford to recover from.
